page: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores running at 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 10.67 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, which includes 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type.

Performance benchmarks indicate highly capable single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression both ranking in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores align with average mid-tier expectations. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth is strong, reaching 254.5 GB/sec, while write bandwidth and small-block read bandwidth remain average. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 345.71 tokens/sec during small-model LLM inference, alongside strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression.

The absence of local storage requires external storage attachments, which may impact sequential I/O-heavy operations depending on network configurations. However, the high memory-to-core ratio and dedicated NVIDIA L4 GPU make this configuration highly suitable for machine learning inference, data science, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks. The shared CPU allocation model presents a potential tradeoff for sustained, non-GPU compute-bound workloads, but the hardware profile remains cost-efficient for memory-intensive and entry-to-mid-level AI workloads.
description: UpCloud GPU-12xCPU-128GB-1xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server designed for GPU-accelerated and memory-intensive workloads. It features 12 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 128.0 GB of RAM, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM. The system lacks local storage, requiring external storage solutions. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core CPU performance and exceptional small-model LLM text generation speeds, alongside strong large-block memory read bandwidth. Multi-core performance and database operations align with mid-tier averages. This configuration is highly suitable for machine learning inference, data science pipelines, and graphics rendering where dedicated GPU acceleration and a high memory-to-core ratio are required.
